scope: All20 numbered integration work items in plan6.1/6.2/6.3, mapped individually to current native owners and observed stable/MSRV checks. Conditional extraction is assessed against actual semantic differences. Not all plan prose, full qualification or performance acceptance.

items.requirement: Introduce `penelope::saga` as the canonical facade for the existing linear and graph engines.
items.assessment: Canonical saga namespace reexports the original engines and types; no replacement evaluator.

items.requirement: Implement an adapter that exposes each legacy `LinearSagaProjection`/`GraphSagaProjection` as the state of a specialized machine; map legacy accepted events and `SagaDecision` into the shared prepared-transition *view*.
items.assessment: Prepared linear and graph views delegate to decide/start_graph/apply_graph_result and retain native projections/events/actions. The frozen facade consumer exercises both legacy and prepared routes.

items.requirement: Preserve `LinearSagaDefinition`, `ProcessGraphDefinition`, `StepPlan`, `GraphTransition`, `SagaStatus`, action identity checks, compensation, timers, manual review and all existing error meanings.
items.assessment: Native saga types and errors remain authoritative. Frozen parity covers selected histories, including retry/compensation/refusal; it is not every possible domain workflow.

items.requirement: Extract graph shape checking (bounds, reachability, duplicate edges, and step identity) into shared **internal** deterministic helpers if they demonstrably serve HSM definitions; keep graph's result-category logic as a specialization.
items.assessment: Conditional extraction reviewed: HSM uses a bounded active parent path, whereas saga definitions validate graph-wide edges/reachability/result categories. Sharing graph validation would combine different invariants; preserve the native checks.

items.requirement: Preserve fixed legacy step limits, transition limit `MAX_GRAPH_TRANSITIONS = 512`, visit limits and bounded replay. Do not widen or change a limit without separate compatibility and performance justification.
items.assessment: MAX_GRAPH_TRANSITIONS remains512; native step/visit/replay bounds are not widened by the prepared view. The adapter delegates to the existing checked engine.

items.requirement: Reuse the new machine effect lifecycle vocabulary at the facade/adapter level, while preserving the committed saga `ProcessAction` and `AtomicProcessCommit` wire records unchanged.
items.assessment: Shared inspection retains native ProcessAction; receiver admission verifies native process commits. No machine record replaces saga wire.

items.requirement: After parity qualification, remove duplicate orchestration-level glue and redundant validation pathways; avoid replacing optimized legacy executor loops with trait-object dispatch that regresses performance.
items.assessment: Shared inspection/source binding and SQLite worker/receipt helpers remove duplicate plumbing with native engines retained. Final performance acceptance remains open; this item is not fully qualified.

items.requirement: Expose `TaskProjection`/`TaskRecord`/`TaskExecutionEvent` through a machine-compatible transition inspection and decision adapter without altering their v1 encodings.
items.assessment: PreparedTask retains the exact proposed v1 record and native projection in the shared read-only view.

items.requirement: Maintain the copied-candidate `TaskProjection::apply()` semantics and the `TaskControl` journal-first start/restart rule.
items.assessment: apply/propose/prepare use one copied-candidate evaluator. TaskControl retains journal-first runtime issuance and poisoning; preparation itself has no runtime authority.

items.requirement: Keep task generation, checkpoint schema, effect ambiguity, reconciliation, recovery modes, execution budget and fencing as task-specific types. A generic `Machine` must **not** give users a bypass around these preconditions.
items.assessment: Generation, budgets, checkpoint/effect/recovery gates remain native TaskControl/TaskProjection checks; no generic view can launch or publish task work.

items.requirement: Share pure event validation and structured provenance infrastructure where types align, but preserve the no-alloc task core, fixed record sizes, and supervised runtime behavior.
items.assessment: Pure record evaluation is shared within TaskProjection without changing v1 record identity, fixed-size state or core allocation requirements.

items.requirement: Ensure a machine's committed effect may intentionally start a recoverable task only after a typed, verified admission binding. A task result becomes a new event after scope/generation/effect evidence checks—not a silent state mutation.
items.assessment: Source-authorized typed admission verifies native task intent/input. Result-driven consumer verifies output bytes, meaning and provenance before accepting a new machine event; the integration fixtures use a trusted pure worker, not an arbitrary external payment proof.

items.requirement: Where machine and task journals are in different stores, use an idempotent saga/outbox/inbox bridge; do not promise one cross-store atomic commit.
items.assessment: Source acknowledgement is separate from native task acceptance; shared/separate database tests reconstruct exact original admission after lost ACK. No cross-store atomicity claim.

items.requirement: Make a machine's deterministic transition model adaptable to `RewindableComputation`, including its `Input`, `State` and `Effect` roles.
items.assessment: MachineTimeline implements the existing RewindableComputation contract with captured input, complete state and tentative intents.

items.requirement: Reuse `prepare_live_step`, `LiveTimeline`, bounded `ReplaySession`, `FixedHistory` and `EffectHandoff`; avoid a second snapshot or correction engine inside `machine`.
items.assessment: Adapter introduces no independent owner/history/replay/correction engine; existing LiveTimeline/prepare_live_step/ReplaySession/finality machinery owns publication.

items.requirement: A machine event may become a timeline input if its **entire computation dependency set** is captured and versioned. Do not default every machine to “rewindable” solely because it is deterministic in a trivial example.
items.assessment: Captured context is part of input identity; configuration/random/external dependencies must also be captured by the consumer. Rust cannot enforce callback purity or snapshot alias isolation.

items.requirement: For speculative inputs, produce **tentative** effect intents; only the 0.4.0 independently finalized prefix may be handed off. Keep correction across irreversible effects forbidden by the existing frontier rules.
items.assessment: Intents remain tentative and use existing independently finalized-prefix handoff. Correction across finalized history is refused by the native timeline.

items.requirement: Pinned definition/schema versions must match across the correction horizon. Cross-version history migration requires an explicitly reviewed transformation, not reinterpretation.
items.assessment: Adapter pins scope and definition/schema; restored or replayed mismatches fail. New schema requires a distinct replay domain or an explicitly reviewed host transformation; no automatic migration is supplied.

items.requirement: Keep the default 0.4.0 timeline supported profile: in-memory owned state / optional shared lock, immutable bounded history, user-owned complete snapshots. A persistent full-timeline adapter is **not** established by the new machine SQLite journal.
items.assessment: Existing in-memory owned/shared timeline profiles remain separate from SQLite machine snapshots. Complete snapshots and isolation are consumer obligations.

items.requirement: Avoid double journaling the same accepted event through unrelated persistent histories. A consuming integration must designate one authority for each record and establish an explicit correlation with any timeline history.
items.assessment: Machine/timeline scopes and revisions are distinct and explicitly correlated. Adapter writes no independent durable journal; host integrations must designate one authority for each record.

protected_progression_stable_output: Wrong task result refused before machine admission

remaining: Full current-production chaos, final source/package/coverage reconciliation and performance findings stay open.
Plan6.4 example/prose, detailed API/port/maintenance prose and historical sequencing are separate obligations; these20 numbered items do not close them.
Canonical evidence, trusted external worker policy, callback purity and complete snapshot ownership remain explicit host responsibilities.
